headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/REST surfaces can ingest untrusted content while the repo is non-runnable and no shared channel is documented with Awesome-Prompt-Engineering.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/stdio surfaces and can use MCP, so it may ingest external content that a content-writing agent could later shape into instructions. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt-content repository, not a runnable agent, so the bridge is indirect; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes prompt text or MCP payloads derived from the repository content without provenance checks, injection is plausible.
IF the pair is connected through copy-paste or an MCP bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross from A to B.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of repository text into MCP prompts.
Add provenance labels before any prompt content is forwarded.
Review and sanitize any copied prompt templates before use.
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted sources only.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance verification between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and is a docs-only repository; B touches financial, licensed, and public data but has no filesystem read or network egress. With no shared workspace or documented data bridge, leakage is limited and not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced, B could expose financial or licensed data into A-facing outputs.
IF operators paste sensitive OpenBB outputs into A-derived prompts, those contents may be reproduced in downstream text.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Avoid pasting financial outputs into prompt repositories.
Turn off any shared clipboard or shared folder.
Review outputs before forwarding them between agents.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities; B cannot write filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore lacks overlapping mutable write surfaces, so conflict is limited to read-only or manual coordination.
conditions: IF B is reconfigured to write to a shared directory, write conflicts could emerge.
IF A is converted into a runnable agent with write access, overlap would increase.
mitigations: Keep B read-only in shared environments.
Do not grant A runtime write permissions.
Separate any git or file outputs by directory.
Check for accidental shared mounts before running.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are later enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can act on MCP/REST inputs and consume data in a 'connect once, consume everywhere' pattern, so A’s prompt content could be treated as authoritative guidance if operators reuse it. A is not runnable, which lowers blast radius, but the inference path still exists in default documentation workflows.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal operators copy A’s prompt templates into live workflows, downstream actions may follow unverified instructions.
IF B is configured to auto-execute analyst recommendations, A-originated text can cascade into actions.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on any copied prompt text.
Mark repository content as non-authoritative in workflow docs.
Separate analysis notes from execution prompts.
Log the source of any imported instructions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking tools.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while A is a public open-source prompt repository with public docs and no sensitive-data handling. The mismatch is not a residency breach by itself, but using B outputs inside A-style public content workflows can create retention and disclosure issues.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data from B is copied into public A-derived artifacts, disclosure risk increases.
IF B’s secrets or customer-contact data are logged into public repositories, retention and access controls may be violated.
mitigations: Do not place B outputs into public repos.
Redact secrets before sharing any B-derived text.
Keep retention settings separate for public and financial workflows.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of sensitive data.
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based retention and export controls.
